about: How a child's name is said (B-42, docs/milestones/B42.md section 3.2): the spelling a parent checked, which the gateway turns into the child's own name clip. Hebrew letters, nikud, a space, a hyphen (ASCII or maqaf) and a geresh (ASCII apostrophe or U+05F3), 1 to 24 UTF-16 units; a mark only on a letter and at most three in a row; no leading, trailing or double space; at least one letter; never U+05B3 or U+05C7, which the voice is never sent. supabase/functions/name_spoken_test.ts asserts _shared/name_spoken.ts (NAME_SPOKEN, NAME_SPOKEN_MAX) equal server_pattern and max_utf16_units and that it takes every accept vector and refuses every reject vector, and child-put takes and refuses the same. app/test/name_spoken_test.dart asserts app/lib/data/child_name.dart (validateSpokenName) gives the same answer for every vector. hash_examples: the first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the UTF-8 spelling, which name-voice answers (spelling_hash) and the phone keys a clip by; both tests check them. The database check (supabase/migrations/20261103120000_name_spoken.sql) is the same rule and is tested by supabase/tests/database/10_name_spoken.test.sql. units: the length in UTF-16 code units, checked by both tests so that an editor cannot change a vector silently.

accept.name: a name with a dagesh and a shva
a shin with a dagesh, a shin dot and a vowel: three marks in a row
first and family name with a space
an ASCII apostrophe as a geresh

reject.name: only combining marks, no base letter
a mark at the start of the name
four marks in a row on one letter
hataf qamats U+05B3 (never sent to the voice)
qamats qatan U+05C7 (never sent to the voice)
a Hebrew punctuation mark, sof pasuq U+05C3
